title: Aave deposits require a non-zero max slippage as a second, independent configuration tripwire
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.7.1.3 adds a check that most other deposit paths do not have: "The operator must ensure a maximum slippage has been configured for the `aToken`. The transaction reverts with `max-slippage-not-set` when `maxSlippages[aToken]` is zero" — `require(maxSlippages[aToken] != 0, ...)`.

The pattern is a **sentinel-zero configuration guard**. Zero is not treated as "no slippage permitted" — it is treated as "nobody has decided yet," and the operation refuses to proceed. This is the safe interpretation of an unset mapping entry in Solidity, where absence and zero are indistinguishable.

What it buys is protection against **partial onboarding**. A venue could plausibly be given a rate limit — which, being the whitelist, makes it usable — without anyone remembering to set its slippage bound. Without this check the first deposit would proceed with an effectively unbounded tolerance. With it, the venue is inert until both parameters exist.

The generalizable rule is worth stating: when permissioning is collapsed into one parameter (as it is here, into the rate limit), every *other* required parameter needs its own presence check, because the single gate no longer guarantees that a full configuration was performed. Consolidating the whitelist into the limit is elegant, but it removes the natural place where a checklist of required settings would have lived.

That this appears on the Aave path in particular is consistent with Aave being one of Grove's largest venue families in the Instance directory, spanning Aave Core v3 and Aave Horizon across several assets and chains.
description: Beyond the rate limit that acts as the whitelist, depositAave reverts with max-slippage-not-set when maxSlippages for the aToken is zero, using a sentinel value to catch half-configured venues.
